learningObjective: Understand the role of the Relax VM in executing compiled TVM programs.

canonicalClaims.claim: The Relax VM is a bytecode-based runtime that dispatches PrimFunc calls, external-library calls, and control flow, and handles dynamic-shape memory allocation and object lifetime. It separates static AOT compilation of tensor programs from dynamic runtime dispatch of graph structure.
nonImplications: Does not imply the VM is the only deployment path.

misconceptions.claim: Relax VM is a Python interpreter that executes IR line-by-line.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is a compiled bytecode VM, not a Python interpreter of IR.

misconceptions.claim: The Relax VM JIT-compiles TensorIR at every function call.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PrimFuncs are AOT-compiled to target code; the VM only dispatches them.

misconceptions.claim: The Relax VM supports only CPU targets.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPU targets are supported via device-side kernels dispatched by the VM.

misconceptions.claim: The VM removes the need for AOT compilation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AOT compilation of PrimFunc is still required; the VM ties compiled artifacts together.

implementationFacts: Bytecode instructions include Call, AllocTensor, AllocStorage, If, Return.
Dynamic-shape allocation is orchestrated by the VM using shape variables.
